findings.title: Interpolation runs before the $__range check, so the no-split guard may stop working
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now interpolates every target with `applyTemplateVariables` (line 299) before `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` at line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep `$__range` queries unsplit, and the comment there says that variable must stay un-interpolated because the backend fills it in for the split time range. If `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range` with a concrete duration, the check no longer matches and such queries get split, producing wrong per-chunk results. The guard should inspect the raw expression, or the interpolation should happen after partitioning for the non-splitting path.

findings.title: Targets are interpolated twice on the shard-splitting path
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates each target here, and every sub-request then calls `runSplitQuery` (line 163 of this file), which interpolates the same targets again at querySplitting.ts line 299. Interpolation is not idempotent: a variable value containing `$` (for example a regex or a literal like `$foo`) gets substituted a second time, and the final query can differ from what the user wrote. The existing test asserting `applyTemplateVariables` was called 5 times is evidence of this repeated work. Interpolate once, at one layer.

findings.title: Test asserts the redundant interpolation call count as expected behavior
findings.body: The assertion changed from 1 call to `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`. That locks in the repeated interpolation (one call in `runShardSplitQuery` plus one per sub-request) as intended behavior rather than catching it. If the double interpolation is fixed, this test will fail for the wrong reason, and it does not check that the interpolated values are correct.

findings.title: No test covers the $__range guard after interpolation moved earlier
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only checks `$__auto` and `$step`. Since interpolation now happens before `querySupportsSplitting`, nothing verifies that a query using `$__range` is still excluded from splitting. The regression described above would go unnoticed.
